author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-18 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Tonight as you dream ask yourself where you are.
context_before: The dreamer in you is God.
context_after: Many times while lying on my bed I have left this body I know so well, to enter a world just as real as this. Remembering where my body was when I started my journey, when I desired to return I had to feel myself in the body – now cataleptic – on the bed. I could not move it or open its eyes. The body felt dead, yet I was very much alive. Gradually I was able to move a finger, then the toes. But only as I opened my eyes and saw the familiar objects on the wall and dresser did I know I was back. But was I really? Am I not dreaming this world just as much as I was dreaming that one? If so then where am I right now?
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from God Speaks To Man (1968-01-18).

quote_original: I have a friend who dreamed it was his birthday and many people had arrived to attend his party.
context_before: A dream contains one central thought. Like a thank you note. You don’t try to interpret every word in it, just the message it is trying to convey.
context_after: There were two large cakes, with one lady very adamant about the design she had placed on hers. (This is not significant to the dream, but only part of getting the story started.) Leaving to find candles for the table, my friend returned to discover one cake was missing, as well as all of the guests. Disappointed because he had not seen or heard me speak, the dream ended. Suddenly he finds himself on a beach with a friend. Asking where everyone was, his friend points to a rock in the middle of the water, and said: “There they are, away out to sea.” Seeing another rock near it supporting a child, afraid and alone, he said: “How did they get there?” and his friend answered: “Mentally.” Then he mentally went to the child, took her by the hand, and placed her on the big rock. Now the dream changes and my friend finds himself in a lecture hall with a stairway in the center of the stage. Coming down the stairs, I place his hands in mine and say: “I’m glad you have made it, chosen one.” Then he awoke.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from God Speaks To Man (1968-01-18).
